title: Templates: Reuse a Recipe
summary: A template is like a recipe with a blank space for the kind of value. One recipe can work with whole numbers or decimal numbers.
introduction: A template is like a recipe with a blank space for the kind of value. One recipe can work with whole numbers or decimal numbers. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Use one function with two kinds of numbers
Make a box that stores one value
Limit a template to whole-number types

blocks.text: T is a name for a type we will choose later. C++ fills it in when we call the function.

blocks.title: templates.cpp

blocks.text: Classes can be templates too. Box<int> stores a whole number. Box<std::string> stores text.

blocks.title: templates.cpp

blocks.text: Set a rule for the type
A concept names a rule for a type. std::integral means a whole-number type. This C++20 function accepts int, but it does not accept a decimal such as 2.5.

blocks.title: templates.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: A template does not make every action work with every type. A type must support the actions used in the recipe.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Call twice(10). Predict the answer before you run it.
